title: Boss: the hot shard incident
summary: From a per-shard dashboard snapshot to a fix: find the hot shard and its skew, verify the backfill before cutting over, salt the celebrity counter, and place keys with rendezvous hashing.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **INC-2291 (sev 2): likes API p99 over 3 s, 5xx on writes.** You are on call. This is the per-shard snapshot
the alert linked to, taken at 20:14 during a live sports final:
shard  range (post_id)       writes/s   cpu   p99 write
top keys on s3 (sampled):  likes:post91822177  71%   likes:post91822180  4%
Two problems stack up: new posts (growing ids) all land on s3, and one viral post takes most of its writes.
The plan agreed in the incident channel:
1. put numbers on the skew for the postmortem;
2. move to hash placement across new shards with a dual-write and backfill, verified before cut over;
3. salt the viral post's like counter;
4. place keys with rendezvous hashing, so adding shards later moves as few keys as possible.
Each task below is one of those steps.

steps.title: 1. Hottest shard and skew
prompt: The snapshot arrives as lines like `s3 writes=6120 cpu=97` (the fields after the name may come in any order).
- `string Hottest(string[] lines)`: the name of the shard with the most writes (the first one on a tie); `""`
when there are no lines.
- `double Skew(string[] lines)`: the hottest shard's writes divided by the **average** writes; `0` when there
are no lines or the average is 0. For the snapshot it is about `3.32`: s3 does 3.3 times its fair share.
solution: if (w > max) { max = w; best = line.Split(' ')[0]; }
hints: Write a small helper that finds the part starting with `writes=` and parses the number after it.
Skew is `max / average`; guard the empty case and an average of zero.
template: {{CODE}}
string[] dojoSnap = { "s0 writes=410 cpu=22", "s1 writes=395 cpu=21", "s2 writes=440 cpu=24", "s3 writes=6120 cpu=97" };
Dojo.Eq("s3 is the hottest", "s3", Hottest(dojoSnap));
Dojo.Eq("s3 does 3.32 times its share", 3.32, Math.Round(Skew(dojoSnap), 2));
string[] dojoEven = { "a writes=100 cpu=10", "b writes=100 cpu=11" };
Dojo.Eq("a tie goes to the first shard", "a", Hottest(dojoEven));
Dojo.Eq("an even cluster has skew 1", 1.0, Math.Round(Skew(dojoEven), 2));
Dojo.Eq("fields in another order", "s9", Hottest(new[] { "s8 cpu=10 writes=20", "s9 cpu=50 writes=70" }));
Dojo.Eq("no lines, no hottest", "", Hottest(new string[0]));
Dojo.Eq("no lines, skew 0", 0.0, Skew(new string[0]));
Dojo.Eq("an idle cluster has skew 0", 0.0, Skew(new[] { "a writes=0 cpu=1", "b writes=0 cpu=1" }));

steps.title: 2. Verify the backfill before cutting over
prompt: Before reads move to the new shards, compare the old data (`source`) with the copy (`target`), key by key.
Write `List<string> Verify(Dictionary<string, string> source, Dictionary<string, string> target)` that returns
one line per problem, ordered by key (ordinal):
- `missing <key>`: in source, not in target (the backfill skipped it);
- `differs <key>`: in both with different values (a write reached only one side);
- `extra <key>`: in target, not in source (a delete reached only one side).
An empty list means it is safe to cut over.
starter: List<string> Verify(Dictionary<string, string> source, Dictionary<string, string> target)
solution: List<string> Verify(Dictionary<string, string> source, Dictionary<string, string> target)
foreach (var key in source.Keys.Union(target.Keys).OrderBy(k => k, StringComparer.Ordinal))
else if (!source.TryGetValue(key, out var original)) problems.Add($"extra {key}");
hints: Walk the union of both key sets, sorted with `StringComparer.Ordinal`.
Check `missing` first, then `extra`, then compare the values.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoSrc = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["a"] = "1", ["b"] = "2", ["c"] = "3", ["d"] = "4" };
var dojoDst = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["a"] = "1", ["b"] = "20", ["d"] = "4", ["e"] = "5" };
Dojo.Eq("one of each problem, by key", new List<string> { "differs b", "missing c", "extra e" }, Verify(dojoSrc, dojoDst));
Dojo.Eq("an exact copy is safe", new List<string>(), Verify(dojoSrc, new Dictionary<string, string>(dojoSrc)));
Dojo.Eq("nothing to copy", new List<string>(), Verify(new Dictionary<string, string>(), new Dictionary<string, string>()));
Dojo.Eq("an empty target misses everything", new List<string> { "missing a", "missing b", "missing c", "missing d" }, Verify(dojoSrc, new Dictionary<string, string>()));
Dojo.Eq("ordinal order: upper case first", new List<string> { "missing B", "missing a" }, Verify(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["a"] = "1", ["B"] = "2" }, new Dictionary<string, string>()));

steps.title: 3. Salt the viral counter
prompt: One post takes 71% of s3's writes. Spread its like counter over several rows.
Write `class SaltedCounter`:
- `SaltedCounter(int buckets)`: throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when `buckets < 1`.
- `string KeyFor(string key, long writeSeq)`: the row a write goes to, `$"{key}#{writeSeq % buckets}"`
(`writeSeq` is never negative).
- `void Add(string key, long writeSeq, long amount)`: add `amount` to that row.
- `long Total(string key)`: the sum over all of the key's buckets (`0` for an unknown key).
- `int RowCount`: how many rows exist so far.
starter: public string KeyFor(string key, long writeSeq) => "";
public void Add(string key, long writeSeq, long amount) { }
solution: public string KeyFor(string key, long writeSeq) => $"{key}#{writeSeq % buckets}";
public void Add(string key, long writeSeq, long amount)
for (var i = 0; i < buckets; i++) total += rows.GetValueOrDefault($"{key}#{i}");
hints: Keep a `Dictionary<string, long>` of rows; `GetValueOrDefault` returns 0 for a row that does not exist yet.
A reader must visit every bucket `#0` to `#(buckets-1)`.
template: var dojoC = new SaltedCounter(4);
for (var dojoI = 0; dojoI < 8; dojoI++) dojoC.Add("likes:post9", dojoI, 1);
Dojo.Eq("eight likes in total", 8L, dojoC.Total("likes:post9"));
Dojo.Eq("spread over four rows", 4, dojoC.RowCount);
Dojo.Eq("write 6 goes to bucket 2", "likes:post9#2", dojoC.KeyFor("likes:post9", 6));
dojoC.Add("likes:post9", 9, 5);
Dojo.Eq("amounts add up", 13L, dojoC.Total("likes:post9"));
Dojo.Eq("still four rows", 4, dojoC.RowCount);
Dojo.Eq("an unknown key is zero", 0L, dojoC.Total("likes:other"));
dojoC.Add("likes:post2", 0, 3);
Dojo.Eq("keys do not mix", 13L, dojoC.Total("likes:post9"));
Dojo.Eq("the other key has its own rows", 3L, dojoC.Total("likes:post2"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("zero buckets is an error", () => new SaltedCounter(0));
{{CODE}}

steps.title: 4. Place keys with rendezvous hashing
prompt: Write `string Rendezvous(string key, string[] shards)`: score every shard with `H.Hash($"{shard}|{key}")` and
return the shard with the **highest** score (the earlier shard wins a tie). Throw `InvalidOperationException`
when there are no shards.
`H.Hash(string)` returning `uint` is given. The tests check that load is even, that removing a shard moves only
its own keys, and that adding a shard moves keys only to the new one.
solution: if (score > bestScore) { best = shard; bestScore = score; }
hints: Start with the first shard as the best, then compare every other shard's score with `>` (so ties keep the earlier one).
Guard the empty array before reading `shards[0]`.
template: {{CODE}}
string[] dojoS = { "s0", "s1", "s2", "s3" };
var dojoKeys = Enumerable.Range(0, 2000).Select(i => $"post:{i}").ToList();
var dojoOwner = dojoKeys.ToDictionary(k => k, k => Rendezvous(k, dojoS));
Dojo.Check("every key lands on a shard", dojoOwner.Values.All(o => dojoS.Contains(o)), "a key landed somewhere else");
Dojo.Eq("the same key always lands on the same shard", dojoOwner["post:7"], Rendezvous("post:7", dojoS));
var dojoShares = dojoOwner.Values.GroupBy(o => o).Select(g => g.Count() / 2000.0).ToList();
Dojo.Check("load is even (each shard 15% to 35%)", dojoShares.Count == 4 && dojoShares.All(s => s > 0.15 && s < 0.35), string.Join(", ", dojoShares.Select(s => s.ToString("P0"))));
string[] dojoWithout = { "s0", "s2", "s3" };
Dojo.Check("removing s1 keeps every other key in place", dojoKeys.Where(k => dojoOwner[k] != "s1").All(k => Rendezvous(k, dojoWithout) == dojoOwner[k]), "a key not on s1 moved");
string[] dojoWith = { "s0", "s1", "s2", "s3", "s4" };
var dojoMoved = dojoKeys.Where(k => Rendezvous(k, dojoWith) != dojoOwner[k]).ToList();
Dojo.Check("adding s4 moves keys only to s4", dojoMoved.All(k => Rendezvous(k, dojoWith) == "s4"), "a key moved between old shards");
Dojo.Check("adding a 5th shard moves about a fifth of the keys (10% to 30%)", dojoMoved.Count > 200 && dojoMoved.Count < 600, $"{dojoMoved.Count} of 2000 moved");
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("no shards is an error", () => Rendezvous("x", new string[0]));
static class H
public static uint Hash(string s)
foreach (var c in s) { h ^= c; h *= 16777619; }
return h;
